docs.title: LRO Narrow Angle Camera, DEM Schrodinger Vent
docs.description: This is a 5m/px digita elevation model (DEM) generated using Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) stereo images and Lunar Orbiter Laser Alimeter(LOLA) shot points from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) mission. Each NAC stereopair was processed to create a multiple DEMs,each DEM was aligned tointersecting LOLA shot points, and merged into a sigle DEM using AIMES Stereo Pipeline.

docs.title: LRO NAC DEM 2.4mpp, Endurance-A Concept Site C
docs.description: This is an LRO (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter) NAC (Narrow Angle Camera) DEM generated using AMES Stereo Pipeline and ISIS4. This data has been generated to resolve the Endurance-A Site <> at a higher resolution. This DEM has been vertically aligned to LOLA (community standard reference). docs.title: LRO NAC and CE-2 CCD DEM, Horseshoe
docs.description: This is an elevation mosaic produced by combining stereo pairs generated from LROC NAC images, for the Horseshoe site in Mare Crisium. Each NAC stereo pair was individually aligned to LOLA laser altimetry. Areas where NACs were not available were filled using Chang'E 2 elevation data. Chang'E 2 data was interpolated to increase resolution to match the NAC images.

docs.title: LRO NAC DEM 2.5mpp, Shioli
docs.description: This Digital Elevation Model (DEM) mosaic of the Shioli region has been generated from individual Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) stereo pair images. DEMs have been individually generated using USGS ISIS7 software. Individual DEMs have been horizontally coregistered to the LRO Wide Angle Camera (WAC) basemap, vertically aligned to Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data, and mosaicked together using ArcGIS Pro. This mosaic has been exported at a 2.5 m/px resolution. Data credit: Heather Lethcoe; NASA’s Solar System Treks Team at Jet Propulsion Laboratory (heather.a.lethcoe@jpl.nasa.gov)

docs.title: LRO LOLA NAC DEM 3.5mpp, IM-1 Landing Site
docs.description: This is a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) mosaic for the Intuitive Machines IM-1 Nova-C, known as Odysseus, lander. This DEM mosaic has been generated using USGS ISIS software from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) imagery. Individual DEMs have been aligned to the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) community standard references and mosaicked together using ArcGIS Pro. Holes in the NAC DEM have been filled with LOLA DEM data. Data is in a orthographic projection and the mosaic is centered at 80.13S 1.44E. Data creator: Heather Lethcoe at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (hlethcoe@jpl.nasa.gov).

docs.title: LRO NAC and CE-2 CCD DEM, Aristarchus Crater
docs.description:
The NASA ARTEMIS Program is a human exploration mission carried out by NASA, US commercial spaceflight companies, ESA, JAXA, and CSA. The program is the next step in establishing a sustainable human presence on the moon amongst other goals. Aristarchus, a young crater with transient features on the Moon, was selected as a site for the Apollo 18 mission and is one of the landing site candidates of the ARTEMIS mission. In order to provide a VR dataset for astronaut training for the mission, the best possible 3D image dataset is needed. Using LROC-NAC stereo-pairs, this data has been constructed using stereo photogrammetry at the very high resolution of 0.5m/px for the orthorectified images (ORI) and a 1m/px Digital Terrain Model (DTM).

The LROC-NAC instrument (Robinson et al., 2010) captures repeat pass single panchromatic grey-scale images at 0.5-2m/px over a swath-width of 2.5-10km with a limited number with suitable stereo angles. Previous authors have applied the SOCET® USGS DTM processing system to individual LROC-NAC stereo-pairs (Henriksen et al., 2017) and a block adjustment of LROC-NAC stereo-pairs is also shown in Haase et al. (2019). It was decided to employ the SELENE+LOLA 59m DTM (Baker et al., 2016) as the basemap as this incorporated the latest processing of LOLA and the selenoid gravity model rather than the global 100m WAC-DTM described in Scholten et al. (2012) which is referenced to Kaguya laser altimeter data. Subsequently, the Chang'e 2 (Wu et al.,2014; Di et al., 2014) stereo-derived 20m DTM (http://moon.bao.ac.cn/index_en.jsp) was employed to provide a steppingstone from the 59m DTM to the 1m DTM.

The DTM data are coaligned and co-registered individually with Chang'e 2 DTM using the ASP function "pc_align". The DTMs are then mosaicked with Chang'e 2 DTM to densify the dataset and fill uncovered areas with LROC-NAC DTMs. The mosaicking was performed using the ASP function "dem_mosaic". The final DTM mosaic has been cropped to JPL’s defined area of interest (AOI). This was done using GDAL function gdalwarp and the respective AOI shapefile.  

This process results in a 1m DTM mosaic of crater Aristarchus on the Moon. Most of the area used stereo-photogrammetrically processing of LROC-NAC stereo-pairs with the UCL CASPGO 3D mapping system and a variety of 3D geospatial handling functions from the NASA ASP function (Beyer, 2015) including height adjustment using ICP between the LROC-DTM and the basemap chosen (Chang'e2 adjusted to SLENE+LOLA). The final DTM mosaic was assessed using the basemap DTMs. Compared against the SELENE+LOLA basemap, the height differences were ∂Z=-0.62±12.95m.

docs.title: LRO LOLA and Kaguya TC DEM 512ppd, Global
docs.description: The LOLA and Kaguya Teams have created an improved lunar digital elevation model (DEM) covering latitudes within ±60°, at a horizontal resolution of 512 pixels per degree (∼59 m at the equator) and a typical vertical accuracy ∼3 to 4 m. This DEM is constructed from ∼4.5×109 geodetically-accurate topographic heights from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) onboard the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, to which we co-registered 43,200 stereo-derived DEMs (each 1×1 degree) from the SELENE Terrain Camera (TC) (∼1010 pixels total). After co-registration, approximately 90% of the TC DEMs show root-mean-square vertical residuals with the LOLA data of <5 m compared to ∼50% prior to co-registration. We use the co-registered TC data to estimate and correct orbital and pointing geolocation errors from the LOLA altimetric profiles (typically amounting to <10 m horizontally and <1 m vertically). By combining both co-registered datasets, we obtain a near-global DEM with high geodetic accuracy, and without the need for surface interpolation. We evaluate the resulting LOLA + TC merged DEM (designated as “SLDEM2015”) with particular attention to quantifying seams and crossover errors. Elevation values are in meters and map values are referred to a radius of 1737400 m.
docs.instrument: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter and Terrain Camera

docs.title: CE-2 CCD DEM
docs.description:
On October 1st, 2010, Chang'E-2 (or CE2) was successfully launched. This was the second Chinese lunar exploration mission. Its main objective was to acquire 1.5m and 7m spatial resolution images at 15km and 100km orbit height. The CE2 Stereo Camera was one of the main payloads of CE2, which used the linear pushbroom scanning technique to capture two-line imagery of forward and backward views along the satellite flight direction; stereo view angles were 7.98deg and -17.2deg respectively. The CCD detector of the camera used a time delayed and integration CCD (TDI CCD), which allowed five integration grades such as 16, 32, 48, 64 and 96, three gains such as 0.7, 1.0 and 2.0. The setting of integration grade was determined by the gain setting, solar illumination condition, the average reflectance of lunar surface and other factors. The spectral range of CCD stereo camera was 450˜ 52m. The image width was 9.2km and 43km, the spatial resolution is 1.5m and 7m with the orbit altitude of 15km and 100km respectively. CE2 Stereo Camera data was used to generate DEM (Digital Elevation Model) and DOM (Digital Orthophoto Map) products for the whole lunar surface. Their ground spatial resolutions are both 7m. The internal precision is reported to be less than two pixels (<14m). Validation of the CE2 global map products was done via comparison of results with five LRRR locations and the LRO WAC DEM. In comparison with LRRR, the planimetric displacement is reported to be 23.9m˜94(stdv 57.2m) in longitude and 9.7m˜53.4m(stdv 37.6m) in latitude, height difference is -1.0m˜18.9m(stdv 10.1m). 2). In comparison with LRO WAC DEM, the average of height difference is reported to be -2.8m, stdv is 116.0m. See “A New lunar global topographic map products from Chang'E-2 Stereo Camera Image Data”, 2014, Ren et al, EPSC Abstracts Vol. 9, EPSC2014-344, European Planetary Science Congress 2014.
The size of this data product download is 256 GB.

docs.title: LRO LOLA DEM, 87.5 deg v4, N Pole
docs.description: This is version 4 of the LRO LOLA DEM, N Pole, 87.5 deg. This data product is a shape map (radius) of the Moon at a resolution 5 meters per pixel, based on altimetry data acquired through September 2011 by the LOLA instrument. The ground tracks were interpolated using the Generic Mapping Tools programs “surface” and “grdblend”. Map values are referred to a radius of 1737400 m.

docs.title: LRO NAC DEM, Peary v2
docs.description: This is a digital elevation model (DEM) extracted from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) stereo images from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission. The original data product is a DEM from stereo images acquired at approximately 1.5 meters/pixel resolution, which allows an output DEM resolution of 4.5 meters/pixel using a softcopy photogrammetry system. However, in some cases, LROC DEMs were also generated at lower resolutions. The DEM was registered horizontally and vertically to LRO's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data. Elevation values are in meters and referred to a radius of 1737400m. Because this area contained many shadows, large areas were covered by using LOLA altimetry shots interpolated using a natural neighborhood interpolation. LOLA altimetry coverage was much sparser than the stereo resolution (for more see the complete section below).
